clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old male presented to the emergency department after a near-fall with a twisting mechanism (slipping on clothing while walking downstairs, twisting backward without striking the ground). Initially pain-free, he developed delayed-onset left-sided flank pain with associated nausea and vomiting while at work, with positional discomfort preventing him from sitting. CT angiography on admission revealed left renal non-enhancement secondary to suspected acute traumatic left renal artery dissection. After multidisciplinary discussion with trauma and vascular surgeons, heparin anticoagulation was initiated in an attempt at renal salvage. The patient was transferred for higher level of care, where angiography confirmed complete lack of flow to the left kidney, consistent with renal artery dissection. Despite anticoagulation and salvage attempts, the patient ultimately required nephrectomy due to renal necrosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Traumatic mechanism consistent with renal artery dissection
Clinical presentation consistent with acute renal injury
Imaging confirmation of left renal artery dissection with non-enhancement
Multidisciplinary surgical consultation and management decision
Confirmatory angiography demonstrating complete vascular occlusion
Definitive outcome with nephrectomy for renal necrosis
